title: Proportional Throughput Remediation: Contract Appendix and Observable SLO Bindings
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a contract appendix and operational playbook that defines proportional remediation tiers for Dedicated throughput guarantees. This doc ties customer-facing SLA language to observable SLO bindings (metrics, windows, measurement method), specifies an error-budget calculation that combines throughput and latency signals, and prescribes a deterministic crediting and notification protocol. The goal is to enable predictable remediation credits, reduce disputes, and provide clear autoscaler interlock behavior for customers on Reserved GPU capacity.
background: Existing throughput SLA drafts focus on single-dimension metrics (tokens/minute or GPU throughput). Customers and Sales have requested (1) clearer measurement artifacts so incident investigations are faster, (2) a remediation schedule that scales with severity, and (3) deterministic interplay between autoscaling actions and crediting. Legal has asked for unambiguous language to reduce arbitration. We observed a high volume of billing disputes tied to ambiguous measurement windows during multi-AZ flaps in the last three reserved-capacity incidents.
proposed_sla_definitions: Offer a tiered SLA: (A) Commit: CommittedTokensPerMinute (CTPM) measured as 1-hour rolling average of successful serving tokens; (B) Latency SLO: P95 completion latency measured at the request boundary; (C) Degradation modes: transient (<5m), sustained (5m-1h), prolonged (>1h). An SLA breach is declared when CTPM < 90% of contracted level OR P95 latency > contracted P95 for the same measurement window. Each breach type maps to a remediation tier.
error_budget_formula: Define an integrated error budget EB over a billing day: EB = (1 - achieved_ratio) * contract_weight + latency_penalty, where achieved_ratio = sum(achieved_tokens_windowed) / sum(committed_tokens_windowed) across rolling 1h windows, contract_weight = 1.0, and latency_penalty = clamp(0,1,(P95_observed / P95_target) - 1) * 0.25. Credits accrue when EB > 0.05 (5%). This hybrid approach ensures small latency regressions don't fully negate throughput guarantees but are weighted into remediation.
measurement_and_monitoring: Primary signal: tokens_served_success_total (per-customer, per-region) aggregated into 1-minute buckets and evaluated as a rolling 1-hour average. Secondary signal: request_latency_ms P95 evaluated over same window. Measurement boundaries exclude requests with user-reported malformed payloads and retries that exceed our documented retry policy. Metric collection uses the existing telemetry pipeline (span tags: customer_id, model_id, region, route). Dashboards and an exportable CSV of the hour-window are required for customer dispute resolution.
remediation_and_crediting_policy:
Proportional crediting tiers (applied to monthly invoice):
- Tier 1 (minor): achieved_ratio between 85% and 90% for >5m -> 5% month-day prorated credit for affected hour windows.
- Tier 2 (moderate): achieved_ratio between 70% and 85% sustained for >15m -> 15% prorated credit plus priority remediation review.
- Tier 3 (severe): achieved_ratio < 70% for any rolling 1h window or prolonged latency breach -> 40% prorated credit and eligibility for one-time capacity make-good (technical remediation session).
Credits are computed proportionally to the delta between committed and achieved tokens, capped by the tier percentage. Credits are additive only across disjoint calendar hours; overlapping windows are de-duplicated by longest-breach rule.
autoscale_interlock_behavior: When an autoscaler initiated by Redwood (not customer-managed) scales down capacity or fails to scale up within a sustained breach window, the event is recorded as 'operator-initiated' and increases measured credit potential by +10% (applied before capping). If customer-managed autoscale rules are in scope and customer did not opt-in to Redwood-managed fallback, then crediting is limited to Tier 1 except by documented exception. The contract appendix includes a toggle clause where customers can opt-in to Redwood-managed autoscale for guaranteed remediation prioritization.
contractual_language_snippet: Appendix: Throughput Remediation and Credits. 'Redwood will measure committed throughput against actual served tokens using a rolling 1-hour window. If actual served tokens fall below the contracted throughput threshold as defined herein, Redwood will provide remediation credits in accordance with the proportional crediting tiers. Credits are subject to verification and will be applied to the next invoice after validation. This appendix supersedes prior informal definitions of throughput guarantee for the duration of the agreement.'
acceptance_criteria: 1) Draft appendix text approved by Legal and Sales; 2) Metrics queries and a verification playbook committed in the runbook repo; 3) Dashboard tile and exportable CSV for customer-facing verification; 4) Automated detection and tagging of breach windows in telemetry with reproducible auditable evidence; 5) Engineering-run smoke test that simulates a sustained 1-hour shortfall and produces expected credit calculation output.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly complex crediting leads to disputes. Mitigation: Provide simple worked examples in the contract and a one-click CSV export for customer verification. Risk: Autoscaler edge-cases produce false positives. Mitigation: Add operator annotations and require cross-check with control-plane scaling logs for credit validation.
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff with Legal and Sales; initial redlines collected.
2025-02-13: Engineering telemetry draft queries (ENG-1842) produced; initial smoke test plan sketched.
2025-02-16: Reviewed hybrid error budget formula with Applied-ML to sanity check latency weighting.
2025-02-18: Legal redline pass complete; preparing PR for internal runbook and contract appendix.
decisions: Adopt hybrid error-budget formula that weights throughput primary and latency secondary (25% weight). Use rolling 1-hour windows for breach detection. Credit tiers as specified. Redwood-managed autoscale opt-in grants enhanced remediation priority.
next_steps: 1) Legal to finalize appendix language by 2025-02-22. 2) ENG to implement detection and CSV export by 2025-02-28. 3) Run smoke test and capture example evidence by 2025-03-02. 4) Release appendix as part of runtime-1.18 contract package.
customer_notes_template: We detected a throughput shortfall for your Dedicated pool on {start} - {end}. Measured achieved_ratio: {ratio}. Based on our contract appendix, your account qualifies for a Tier {tier} credit of {credit_percent}% applied to your next invoice. Attached: hour-window CSV and scaling/orchestration logs for verification.
legal_followups: Legal requested explicit exclusion language for customer-initiated load-testing and for force-majeure events. Also requested a formal dispute-resolution flow with 30-day remediation window. Incorporated into draft appendix.
